passage: I sit behind Hrithik in class, so I saw the whole thing. For about two months he and Pankaj talked every single day, and Hrithik would grin at his phone under the desk. Then Pankaj just stopped. No fight that I know of. Hrithik still kept the phone face up, checking it in every break. He looked pale. At lunch he said, "It's like I was never there," and then went quiet. His cousin told him to make a fake account to see Pankaj's page. Hrithik laughed and said no, that would be weird. Four of us have taken him to the ground since. I can't say what's really in his head, but he seems to be grieving something. I just know he's not sitting alone.

qa.q: For how long did Hrithik and Pankaj talk every day before it stopped?
qa.a: They talked every single day for about two months.

qa.q: What might Hrithik be feeling, and what makes the classmate say so?
qa.a: He may be hurt and grieving. He keeps the phone face up, looks pale, and says, "It's like I was never there," though the classmate admits they cannot be sure what is in his head.

qa.q: What did Hrithik and his friends do that was healthy?
qa.a: Hrithik refused his cousin's idea of a fake account, and his classmates took him to the ground so he has company.

qa.q: How might Pankaj's silence look from Hrithik's side?
qa.a: It feels like erasure, as if the daily talks did not count. The silence probably says more about Pankaj avoiding than about Hrithik's worth.

grounding: After daily talks a crush vanished on Hrithik, seen by a classmate, who notes his hurt, his refusal of a fake account and his friends' company.

passage:
At the coaching hostel in Kota, everyone knew Rajni and Wasim talked every night on the common room phone and messaged all day. Then, one Monday, nothing. He stopped replying. He looked away in the corridor.
By Thursday Rajni felt like she'd been erased. She checked her phone every minute. At night she whispered to her roommate Sunita, "Maybe I'll make a new account. Just to see if he's online."
"No," Sunita said. "That will only hurt you more."
"Then what did I do wrong?"
"Maybe nothing. Some people vanish because they can't handle saying things. That's about him, not you."
Rajni cried into her pillow. Sunita didn't leave. The next evening, two other girls from their floor came to Rajni's room with chai and cards. They played until lights-out. Rajni still checked her phone once or twice. But the new account never got made.

qa.q: Where did Rajni and Wasim talk every night?
qa.a: On the common room phone at the coaching hostel in Kota.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel when Wasim vanished?
qa.a: She felt hurt and erased, anxiously checking her phone every minute and wondering what she had done wrong.
Listening to Sunita, grieving openly instead of making a fake account, and spending time with friends who came with chai and cards.

qa.q: How does Sunita see Wasim's silence?
qa.a: Sunita sees it as Wasim's avoidance, a way of not facing hard conversations, rather than proof that Rajni did something wrong.

grounding: A teen whose crush vanished feels erased, sees it reflects his avoidance, grieves and leans on friends instead of spying.

passage:
Dear Chinmay Dada,
You said I could write to you about anything, so I'm writing about Ritika.
For two months, we messaged every day. Morning and night. She sent me songs; I sent her terrible jokes. Then ten days ago she just stopped. No goodbye. She hasn't even left the chat. It's like I never existed.
I keep thinking I must be really boring or something. I even thought of making a fake profile to check if she's online talking to other people. I didn't do it. I know it's creepy, and it would only hurt more.
Mummy says it's probably about Ritika not knowing how to say she's lost interest, not about me. Maybe she's right. It still hurts like crazy.
Can you come over this Sunday? We could play carrom like before. I don't really want to be alone with this.
Your cousin-brother,
Abhinav

qa.q: How long did Abhinav and Ritika message every day?
What is Abhinav feeling about Ritika's silence?
qa.a: Abhinav feels deeply hurt and erased, as if he never existed, and fears he is boring.

qa.q: Which choices show Abhinav is handling this wisely?
qa.a: He did not make a fake profile, he listened to Mummy's view that it's about Ritika's avoidance, and he is asking his cousin for company.

qa.q: How might Chinmay Dada feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Chinmay Dada is likely touched to be trusted and wants to cheer his cousin up with a Sunday carrom game.

grounding: A teen whose crush vanished after daily messages feels erased, avoids spying, and asks a cousin for company.
